core_obligations: Start from the degreewise homotopy relation alpha = beta + dh + hd and the homotopy h with its components h^n from L^n to M^{n-1} (proof lines 14120-14121).

Define the total homotopy H in degree n as the direct sum over a + b = n of h^a tensor the identity of P^b, mapping the n-th piece of the total complex of L tensor P to the n-th piece of the total complex of M tensor P (proof lines 14121-14127).

Verify the homotopy identity Tot(alpha tensor id) = Tot(beta tensor id) + dH + Hd by the degreewise computation, and conclude that the construction descends to the homotopy category (proof lines 14128-14136).

difficulty_reason: The lemma makes the derived tensor product well defined: if two maps of complexes alpha and beta are homotopic, then their totalisations after tensoring with the identity of a fixed complex P are homotopic, so that L to Tot(L tensor P) descends to the homotopy category (statement lines 14103-14117). The proof is short but it is the standard construction rather than a citation (proof lines 14120-14136): from a homotopy h with alpha = beta + dh + hd in each degree one forms the total homotopy H given in degree n by the direct sum of the h^a tensor the identity on P^b over all decompositions n = a + b, and then verifies that Tot(alpha tensor id) equals Tot(beta tensor id) plus dH plus Hd. The verification is described by the author as a straightforward computation, and the only structural point is that summing the degreewise homotopies over the bigraded pieces of the total complex does produce a homotopy of the total complex, which is exactly why the total differential has the shape it has.
